pool.text: General John Forbes named Pittsburgh in honor of British statesman William Pitt.
The General Assembly enacted legislation to incorporate Pittsburgh as a borough.
Pittsburgh has hosted the world's first Mercy Hospital since this year.
The Pennsylvania Railroad first opened service between Pittsburgh and Philadelphia.
The national Republican Party held its first convention here in February.
Andrew Carnegie opened the Pittsburgh Locomotive and Car Works to manufacture for the industry.
Democrats have been elected consecutively to the mayor's office since this election.
The city suffered severe flooding during the month of March.
Duquesne reached the NCAA tournament Final Four once.
The first community-sponsored television station was established on April 1.
Duquesne won the NIT title in its second straight trip to the game.
Jonas Salk developed a successful polio vaccine that came into use.
The Civic Arena opened following the displacement of residents and businesses.
The Pittsburgh Penguins professional hockey team began playing in the city.
The Pittsburgh Pipers won the first American Basketball Association championship led by Connie Hawkins.
The Pirates became the first Major League team to field an all-minority lineup.
Renaissance II launched with a focus on cultural and neighborhood development.
UPMC announced a major expansion and hired transplant pioneer Thomas Starzl.
INPEX, the world's largest invention trade show, began hosting conventions.
High lead levels in drinking water sparked criticism toward the water authority.
